newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Kabila says Mobutu must go before Zaire elections.
newsitem.headline: Kabila says Mobutu must go before Zaire elections.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Tuesday rejected calls for pluralist elections to end Africa's latest war, saying polls could only be held after President Mobutu Sese Seko stepped down or was overthrown.
Kabila, speaking shortly before talks with U.S. envoy Bill Richardson, told Reuters that even then Mobutu and his "corrupt entourage cannot take part in such a process".
Richardson told reporters on arrival in Lubumbashi earlier on Tuesday that elections and the rule of law were necessary to end the war in Africa's third largest country.
But in hard-hitting remarks before meeting Richardson, Kabila said: "There will be no compromise over the departure, through the battlefield or at talks, of Mobutu, his system and his henchmen."
Kabila has agreed to meet Mobutu on a ship off the Atlantic coast to discuss the departure of Africa's longest serving ruler.
Kabila said his troops were advancing on the road to Kinshasa after capturing the town of Kikwit on Tuesday.
